newsitem.title: SWEDEN: FORECAST-MODO 9 MO PROFIT TO DIVE 48 PCT.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-MODO 9 MO PROFIT TO DIVE 48 PCT.

text.p: Swedish forestry group Modo was
expected to post a sharply lower profit after financial items
for the first nine months of 1996 of 2.24 billion crowns, a
Reuter poll of 14 analysts found on Thursday.
Forecast varied between 1.93-2.50 billion crowns.
In the same period a year ago the company reported a profit
after financial items of 4.32 billion crowns.
In the first half of 1996 the company posted a profit of
1.66 billion crowns which means analysts expected a third
quarter profit of 579 million crowns.
For the full year 1996 the average forecast was for a profit
after financial items of 2.70 billion crowns compared to 5.22
billion in 1995.
The average forecast for the full year was 100 million
crowns lower than when Reuter last polled analysts over MoDo
before the half year report.
For 1997 analysts saw MoDo posting a profit of 2.01 billion
crowns.
Analysts in August forecast next year's profit after
financial items at 2.58 billion.
Analysts interviewed for the poll were from Aros, Carnegie,
Enskilda, Fiba, James Capel, Kleinwort Benson, Matteus, Merrill
Lynch, Morgan Stanley, Nordbanken, Nordiska, Salomon, Swedbank,
and Ohman.
MoDo will release its nine month report on November 13.
(Million crowns) AVG RANGE ANALYSTS
-- Peter Fellman, Stockholm newsroom +46-8-700 1007
